facts.statement: The genus Arpagodus was first described by St. John and Worthen in 1875.
The genus Arpagodus currently contains only the single species A. rectangulus.
facts.quote: It currently contains only the species A. rectangulus.

facts.statement: Fossils of Arpagodus are known mainly from the Pennsylvanian subperiod, including sites in Russia and the Raytown Limestone Formation in Kansas, USA.
facts.quote: It is known mainly from the Pennsylvanian subperiod, such as the early Pennsylvanian of Russia and the late Pennsylvanian of Raytown Limestone Formation of Kansas, USA.

facts.statement: Arpagodus belongs to the parent group Helicoprionidae.
Arpagodus is classified within the family Helicoprionidae.
Arpagodus is classified in the class Chondrichthyes.

rejected.statement: Arpagodus is an extinct genus of eugeneodont fish that lived during the Carboniferous period.
rejected.quote: Arpagodus is an extinct genus of eugeneodont fish from the Carboniferous period.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'Arpagodus is an extinct genus of eugeneodont fish'
